title: Archduke by Rajiv Joseph at Roundabout #archdukeplay #rajivjoseph #ro...
transcript: I went to Archduke to see Patrick Page, but stayed for Kristine Nielsen. This new dark comedy by Rajiv Joseph reimagines the circumstances surrounding the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand. But honestly, you don't need to be familiar with the history to follow or appreciate this play. It's just the chosen backdrop for what I feel like is more of a universal story that speaks to how young men can become radicalized. In this play, we see three young men searching for meaning who, upon entering the orbit of Patrick Page's character, show themselves to be quite malleable. The themes are specific but the play doesn't feel arduously burdened by them — the scope is kept in check and the plot shines through, no problem. I don't know how this will hit for everyone because the humor is kind of bizarre, somewhat exaggerated, and even silly with hints of absurdism, but I enjoyed it. I thought the writing was sharp and the performances were great. Kristine Nielsen, despite not having a lot of stage time, gets the opportunity to make the funniest faces that really define the tone of the comedy here. And of course, Patrick Page does not disappoint with his blend of stoicism and relentlessly commanding presence. One thing I was a little iffy on was the overall pacing which I imagine will continue to improve over the preview process. But with it only being two hours including intermission, and Act 2 not currently maintaining the momentum created in Act 1, I'd be curious about if this play would work as a one-act. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
